title: NYC woman returns to site where husband's remains were found: 'Bittersweet' - NewsBreak
text:
1 hours ago
QUEENS, N.Y. (PIX11)– Richard “Max” Albright disappeared from his job, his wife, and his home four years ago in a case PIX11 News first reported in November 2021.
Last week, his remains were discovered in a remote, off-limits area of College Point, Queens.
Despite the relief of finally finding him, his wife now fears foul play.
More Local News She returned to the site for the first time with PIX11 News, still searching for answers.
“There are lots of ‘No Trespassing’ signs — there’s barbed wire,” DiLorenzo asked. “Is this something your husband would ever ignore?”
“Absolutely not,” said Cathi Albright. “He respected everyone — property and laws.”
A four-year journey of worry and wonder has led Cathi here for the first time — to a sprawling vacant lot across from big box stores in College Point.
“It’s bittersweet,” she said.
It’s where her missing husband — Richard, who she calls “Max” — was finally found last week. His remains, reduced to bones, were discovered by a survey crew deep in the densely wooded area off 20th Avenue.
“If he entered here off 20th Avenue, it’s a 20-minute walk through woods and boulders — that’s how it was put to me,” she said.
It’s a trek she believes would have been nearly impossible for Max, given his physical limitations.
The 69-year-old registered nurse was last seen on video shuffling out of the couple’s Queens apartment to run errands.
More: Latest News from Around the Tri-State He left in his slippers — his wife says his feet were throbbing — and then vanished without a trace.
His wife of three decades worked with detectives, a private investigator, and strangers online, desperate for help finding him.
“The unknowing was the hardest part the whole time,” Albright, 62, said.
The medical examiner apparently found no obvious trauma, Albright was told, and the cause of death is listed as “pending further studies.” Investigators found Max’s belongings — including his wallet — nearby.
But this week, the widow learned something new. “His brother told me he pulled out such a wad of cash that he should warn Max — you’re going to get robbed,” she said.
She believes that could be the only reasonable explanation for his death — though she may never know for sure.
